summary.text: Sea ice is frozen seawater floating on the ocean, and it covers about 7% of Earth's surface and about 12% of its oceans.
The polar ice packs reach their greatest extent in winter and retreat in summer, and satellites show a marked decline in Arctic sea ice extent and thickness in recent decades.
Its white surface reflects the Sun's energy back to space and it insulates the ocean below, so its presence or absence shapes climate, regional weather and ocean circulation.

facts.label: Yearly cycle
facts.value: Greatest in winter, retreats in summer

facts.label: Age stages
facts.value: New ice, nilas, young ice, first-year, old

items.prompt: Seawater freezes on a calm polar bay. Why does the new ice stay on top instead of sinking?

options.label: Salt in the ice makes it heavier than water
Wind pressure holds the ice up at the surface
Ice is less dense than the liquid water below
Trapped sunlight keeps the ice warm and buoyant

items.explain: Ice is less dense than liquid water, so sea ice floats just as freshwater ice does.

items.prompt: A warm summer melts a wide stretch of polar sea ice, leaving dark open water. What changes about the Sun's energy there?

options.label: Less of it is reflected back out to space
More of it is reflected back out to space
None of it reaches the ocean surface anymore
It is reflected exactly as much as before

items.explain: The white ice surface reflects the Sun's energy and helps keep the planet cool; losing it means less energy bounces back.

items.prompt: A sheet of sea ice is frozen firmly to the coastline and does not move with currents or wind. What is it called?

options.label: Drift ice
Fast ice
Pack ice
An iceberg

items.explain: Sea ice attached to the shore is landfast or fast ice, as in fastened; drift ice is free to move.

items.prompt: A huge chunk breaks off the front of a glacier and floats out to sea. Does it count as sea ice?

options.label: Yes, any ice floating in the ocean is sea ice
Yes, once it drifts away from the coastline
No, sea ice must be at least a year old
No, it is an iceberg, not frozen seawater

items.explain: Sea ice forms when seawater freezes, while icebergs are pieces of glaciers or ice shelves that calve into the ocean.

items.prompt: In winter a lid of sea ice covers a polar sea. What does it do to the exchange between the water and the air above?

options.label: It speeds up the release of heat into the air
It has no effect on what passes between them
It limits the flow of heat, vapour and gases
It pulls extra carbon dioxide down into the sea

items.explain: Sea ice insulates the ocean, limiting the transfer of heat, water vapour and gases such as carbon dioxide between sea and air.

items.prompt: Roughly how much of Earth's entire surface is covered by sea ice?

options.label: Less than 0.5%
About 7%
About 30%
About half

items.explain: Sea ice covers about 7% of Earth's surface and about 12% of the world's oceans.
